correctness.rationale: All graph assumptions and small 2x2 boundary are explicit. In diameter-two rook graphs, a forbidden geodesic triple is exactly an induced P3; line-graph cliques of the triangle-free K_{m,n} correspond to star components. The three maximal-star-forest cases are necessary and sufficient by edge-addition analysis. Bivariate labeled exponential formulas follow from the unambiguous connected-component species with isolated original vertices. Component counts prove every and only asserted cardinalities. Associated Stirling partitions and two-center configurations give boundary coefficients. A standalone exact checker independently tests 104272 subsets and 41 additional parameter pairs; finite tests supplement the complete proof.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge comparison with full primary texts separates known scalar extrema (m and m+n-2) and the preexisting diameter-two clique characterization from the new complete labeled polynomials, three-class maximality criterion, exact spectrum with arbitrarily long holes, and extremal multiplicities. Focused research-record and bibliographic searches did not find a stronger equivalent; non-exhaustiveness of discovery remains a documented risk.
residual_risks: Search indexes are incomplete; another publication may contain equivalent star-forest counts or full rook-graph general-position distributions.
The generic cluster characterization predates the present work; novelty pertains to the exhaustive maximality classification and exact enumeration, not that known criterion.

value.rationale: The lower general-position number alone does not describe the possible cardinalities of locally maximal configurations. The new full spectrum has arbitrarily long forbidden intervals already in the natural two-row rook graph K_2 square K_n, and both complete labeled polynomials and boundary multiplicities resolve which maximal sizes and how many examples occur. This is a structural and complete-family enumeration motivated by the 2023 lower-parameter work and 2024 general-position polynomial framework, rather than a mere restatement of known scalar extrema.
